doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Grimes's encouragers and the bass player's role
summary: Grimes cites Max Roach and Prez as encouragers; they discuss what the bassist listens to.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Henry, was there somebody in your past that you really felt that set you on — or helped you on your musical career and your path that you were trying to take?

Yes, a lot of professional musicians like Max Roach or the Prez, you know a lot of musicians like that I’ve played with and you know I’d have to go through my struggle up there, which they encouraged me about that.

I always felt like the bass player had a lot of responsibility. Because first, I mean if you don’t know the tune, who’s going to hear it? A saxophone player can sort of negotiate things by listening to the bass player. But who’s the bass player listening to?

Yeah well the bass player is listening to everybody including the drummer and everybody else that’s playing something into it. But for instance like lately I’ve been listening to bass players that don’t — they stop playing what they think musicians hear when you play, like I mean it’s just like they hear any music at all, any sheet music or anything that has notes on it and nothing, and it might be something that they never heard of, you know, just like he says, told him to come up there and get on the stand and play. You know a lot of those things are part of the challenge, it might come to you anyway.
